label: verify-pp-fish-biomechanics-morphology

claims.claim: Harris (Boston) co-authored a verified 2021 Current Biology paper on flying-fish fins
claims.source_says: Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes; Current Biology, Nov 2021; authors Daane, Blum, Lanni, Boldt, Iovine, Higdon, Johnson, Lovejoy, Matthew P. Harris.
claims.note: Crossref confirms the title, journal, year and Harris as last author; the Boston affiliation is not in this record but the claim's core holds.

claims.claim: Lauder's lab has verified 2023-2024 fish swimming and fin papers
claims.source_says: In-line swimming dynamics revealed by fish interacting with a robotic mechanism; eLife, 6 Feb 2023; authors Robin Thandiackal, George Lauder (Harvard University).
claims.note: The cited DOI confirms only one 2023 Lauder paper; the 2024 papers were not opened by me, so the 2023-2024 range rests on other DOIs.

claims.claim: The flying-fish gliding aerodynamics work found is outside Boston
claims.source_says: Aerodynamic characteristics of flying fish in gliding flight; J Exp Biol 2010; Park and Choi, School of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, Seoul National University, Korea.
claims.note: The cited paper is from Seoul, so it is outside Boston; it says nothing on the wider claim that no Boston gliding work exists.

overall: Of the three key claims, two are supported and one is partly supported. I checked all three against Crossref records only. For the Lauder claim, I confirmed one 2023 paper but did not open the 2024 DOIs.
